summary.text: The formalized word is truncated after ten substitutions; since each symbol produces at most four symbols, there are at most \(4^{10}\) detected zeros, so at \(n=4^{10}+1\) the out-of-range enumeration gives \(a(n)=1\). Since \((3+\sqrt3)/3\ge1\), this yields \(nr-a(n)\ge4^{10}>2\), violating the upper bound.

full_proof.text:
Let the substitution be
\[
\sigma(0)=01,\qquad \sigma(1)=0100.
\]
Starting from the one-letter word \(W_0=0\), define finite words recursively by
\[
W_{j+1}=\sigma(W_j),
\]
where the substitution is applied to every letter of \(W_j\) and the resulting words are concatenated.

The proposition under consideration represents the word by using only the tenth iterate \(W_{10}\). More precisely, define a function \(v:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) by
\[
v(k)=
\begin{cases}
\text{the letter of }W_{10}\text{ at zero-based index }k,&k<|W_{10}|,\\
1,&k\ge |W_{10}|.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every index outside the finite word is assigned the default value \(1\), rather than being read from a later substitution iterate.

For a predicate \(P\) on the nonnegative integers, write \(\operatorname{nth}_P(m)\) for the zero-based \(m\)-th nonnegative integer satisfying \(P\). In the definition used here, if there are not enough integers satisfying \(P\), this expression has fallback value \(0\). The proposed zero-position sequence is then
\[
a(n)=\operatorname{nth}_{v(k)=0}(n-1)+1.
\]
The subtraction and the final addition implement the conversion between the one-based indexing of the OEIS sequence and the zero-based indexing of the finite word.

We first bound the number of possible zero positions. Each substituted letter has image of length at most four: \(|\sigma(0)|=2\), \(|\sigma(1)|=4\), and, under the stated rule on natural-number symbols, every other symbol has empty image. Consequently,
\[
|W_{j+1}|=\sum_{x\text{ a letter of }W_j}|\sigma(x)|\le 4|W_j|.
\]
Since \(|W_0|=1\), induction gives
\[
|W_j|\le 4^j
\]
for every \(j\ge0\). Indeed, the claim is true at \(j=0\), and if \(|W_j|\le4^j\), then
\[
|W_{j+1}|\le4|W_j|\le4\cdot4^j=4^{j+1}.
\]
In particular,
\[
|W_{10}|\le4^{10}.
\]

Set
\[
M=4^{10}=1{,}048{,}576.
\]
If \(v(k)=0\), then necessarily \(k<|W_{10}|\): for every \(k\ge|W_{10}|\), the definition gives \(v(k)=1\). Hence every integer satisfying \(v(k)=0\) belongs to
\[
\{0,1,\ldots,M-1\}.
\]
There are exactly \(M\) integers in this set, so there are at most \(M\) integers \(k\) for which \(v(k)=0\).

Now choose
\[
N=M+1=4^{10}+1=1{,}048{,}577.
\]
Then \(N-1=M\). The value \(\operatorname{nth}_{v(k)=0}(M)\) asks for the zero-based \(M\)-th solution of \(v(k)=0\), which would be the \((M+1)\)-st such solution in ordinary one-based language. But there are at most \(M\) solutions. Therefore the requested occurrence does not exist, and by the fallback convention in the definition,
\[
\operatorname{nth}_{v(k)=0}(M)=0.
\]
It follows that
\[
a(N)=0+1=1.
\]

It remains to check the claimed inequality at this positive integer \(N\). Let
\[
r=\frac{3+\sqrt3}{3}.
\]
Because \(\sqrt3\ge0\),
\[
r=1+\frac{\sqrt3}{3}\ge1.
\]
Since \(N>0\), multiplication by \(N\) preserves this inequality, giving \(Nr\ge N\). Using \(a(N)=1\), we obtain
\[
Nr-a(N)=Nr-1\ge N-1=M=4^{10}.
\]
In particular \(Nr-a(N)>2\) (indeed, it is at least \(1{,}048{,}576\)). Thus the upper half of the conjectured two-sided bound,
\[
Nr-a(N)<2,
\]
is false. Equivalently,
\[
\left|Nr-a(N)\right|\not<2.
\]
Therefore it is not true, for this definition of \(a\), that every integer \(n\ge1\) satisfies
\[
-2<\frac{3+\sqrt3}{3}n-a(n)<2.
\]
The explicit counterexample is \(n=4^{10}+1\).

This disproof depends essentially on the finite-prefix definition above: after \(W_{10}\), all word values are set equal to \(1\), so the resulting set of zero positions is finite and the occurrence-enumeration function eventually falls back to \(0\). It therefore disproves the stated finite-prefix proposition. By itself, it does not assert that the same \(n\) is a counterexample for the genuine infinite fixed point of \(0\mapsto01\), \(1\mapsto0100\), whose values beyond \(W_{10}\) would instead be obtained from later substitution iterates.
